title: SFT chat-template packing with truncation
scenario: Normalise vendor chat transcripts (role aliases, merged turns, order checks), truncate to a token budget by dropping the oldest user/assistant pairs, render the training template and summarise tags.

verified.why_correct: `body[2:]` drops exactly one user/assistant pair (the body always alternates after check_order), the system message is kept outside the loop, and `len(body) > 2` stops before the last pair, after which a still-too-long example is rejected, as rules 5 and 6 say.

bugs.title: Numeric 0 content treated as missing
bugs.why: `value or ""` replaces every falsy value, so the assistant's numeric answer 0 in c03 becomes an empty string and the conversation is rejected as empty_message. Only None should become empty.
hints: c03 is rejected as empty_message. Look at its assistant message in the data.
Look at how loader.clean_content handles values that are not strings.
Only treat None as empty: `if value is None: return ""`, then `str(value).strip()`.
probes: Which other JSON values would `or ""` also have swallowed?
Why did c10 stay rejected after the fix?

bugs.title: Rendered parts accumulate across examples
bugs.new:
def render(messages, parts=[]):
    """Chat-template text for one example; every assistant turn is closed with <|end|>."""
bugs.why: A default argument is evaluated once, when the function is defined, so every call without `parts` appends to the same list. Each example's text contains every example rendered before it.
hints: c05's text starts with the math tutor prompt from c01. Where does that come from?
Look at the parts argument of render().
Default to None and create a new list inside: `parts = [] if parts is None else parts`.
probes: Why were the token counts right even though the text was not?
Would c01's text have looked right with this bug? Why?

bugs.title: Blank tags counted as a tag
bugs.old: return [t.strip().lower() for t in text.split(",") if t.strip()]
bugs.why: "".split(",") returns [""], not [], and "math,  " gives a blank second piece. Without the filter those blanks are counted as a tag named "".
hints: tag_counts has a key that is an empty string. Which conversations produce it?
Look at split_tags in reports.py, and try "".split(",") in a REPL.
Keep only non-empty pieces: add `if t.strip()` to the comprehension.
probes: Why does "".split() (no argument) behave differently from "".split(",")?
Why are rejected conversations' tags counted here at all?

context_qa.q: What does build_example() do to one conversation?
context_qa.a: It calls `normalise_roles` (lower-case, alias, reject unknown roles or empty content), then `merge_consecutive`, then `check_order`, and finally returns the result of `truncate`, which is `(messages, dropped_pairs)`. Any rule failure raises `Rejected` with the reason as its message.
It is in loader.py and turns the raw `content` value of a message into the string stored on `Message.content`. Its result is what normalise_roles later tests for emptiness.

context_qa.q: How does check_order handle the system message?
context_qa.a: If the first message is `system`, it is skipped. Any other `system` message raises `misplaced_system`. The rest must alternate user/assistant starting with user, and the last must be assistant, otherwise `bad_order`.
`count_tokens` sums `len(content.split()) + overhead` over the messages, with overhead taken from `per_message_overhead` in config.json (4).

context_qa.q: Where is the template text produced, and is it used for token counting?
context_qa.a: `render.render` builds the text from a list of parts and joins it. The token count in the report comes from `count_tokens` on the messages, not from the rendered text.

context_qa.q: Which conversations does the summary look at?
context_qa.a: `sources` and `tag_counts` are computed over every conversation loaded from the file, kept or rejected. `longest_example` looks only at the kept examples.
